title: Adjectives with Prepositions: Qualities and Relationships
summary: Choose prepositions after adjectives when describing abilities, emotions, awareness, similarity, dependence, interest and responsibility. Learn common adjective patterns as complete phrases rather than applying one general rule.
learningObjectives: Use adjective + of to talk about fears, pride, awareness, capability and typical behaviour.
Use good/bad at to describe ability and distinguish this from interest in an activity.
Contrast similar to, different from or to, dependent on and independent of.
Select on, in, for, with and to in everyday adjective phrases and follow prepositions with nouns or -ing forms when appropriate.

explanation.heading: Feelings, knowledge and capacity with of
explanation.body: Afraid, frightened and terrified of identify what causes fear. Proud of, ashamed of and jealous of name the person or thing connected with a feeling. Aware of describes knowing that something exists; capable of means having the ability to do it. Typical of names behaviour you expect from a particular person or group. When a verb follows a preposition, use its -ing form: capable of managing, not capable of manage.
explanation.example: The new volunteers are capable of organising the event without supervision.

explanation.heading: Ability uses at, but interest uses in
explanation.body: Use good, excellent, bad or hopeless at a skill or activity. A skill can be expressed as a noun or an -ing phrase: good at puzzles; good at solving puzzles. Use interested in to describe curiosity or a desire to learn, whether or not someone is skilled. Fond of means liking someone or something, while keen on expresses enthusiasm for an activity or idea.
explanation.example: Noah is interested in pottery but is still quite bad at shaping clay.

explanation.heading: Similarity, difference and personal dependence
explanation.body: Similar to introduces what something resembles. Different from is a widely accepted choice; different to is also used, especially in British English. Do not use similar with or similar than for this meaning. Dependent on identifies a person or resource needed for support, whereas independent of emphasises freedom from that support. These pairs are not interchangeable simply because their adjectives are opposites.
explanation.example: The revised plan is similar to the original but independent of the earlier budget.

explanation.heading: Responsibility, reputation and certainty
explanation.body: Responsible for names a duty or the cause of a result. Famous for identifies the quality or achievement that made someone or somewhere well known. Certain or sure of and certain or sure about both introduce a fact you believe; in questions or negatives, either may be natural. Suspicious of and critical of show mistrust or disapproval. Tolerant of describes accepting behaviour or ideas even when you dislike them.
explanation.example: The shift supervisor is responsible for checking the emergency exits.

explanation.heading: With, of and to in states and personal relationships
explanation.body: Crowded with introduces the people or objects occupying a space, but full of introduces what fills it. Short of identifies something that is lacking, such as staff or time. Married to or engaged to names a partner; married with two children is different, describing family circumstances, not the partner. Combine these fixed expressions with the correct meaning rather than choosing a preposition based on its usual spatial sense.
explanation.example: The waiting area was crowded with travellers, but the information desk was short of staff.

comparisons.title: Having a skill versus wanting to learn

left.label: good at
left.example: Rosa is good at designing posters.
left.note: At introduces an activity she performs well.

right.label: interested in
right.example: Rosa is interested in designing websites.
right.note: In introduces an activity that attracts her attention, not necessarily one she can do well.

comparisons.title: What you rely on versus freedom from it

left.label: dependent on
left.example: The garden is dependent on regular watering.

right.label: independent of
right.example: The new office is independent of the main building.
right.note: Of names something that the office does not rely on.

examples.sentence: The actor felt proud of her first successful performance.
examples.note: Proud of names the achievement that caused her feeling.

examples.sentence: I was not aware of the change to the train timetable.
examples.note: Aware of identifies information the speaker did not know.

examples.sentence: Their daughter is brilliant at remembering faces.
examples.note: An -ing activity follows the preposition at.

examples.sentence: The new logo is similar to the one on our old website.
examples.note: Similar is followed by to, not with.

examples.sentence: The exhibition is famous for its unusual paper sculptures.
examples.note: Famous for identifies what makes the exhibition notable.

commonMistakes.incorrect: He is very good in explaining difficult ideas.
commonMistakes.correct: He is very good at explaining difficult ideas.
commonMistakes.why: Good at introduces a skill, and explaining correctly follows the preposition.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Their timetable is similar with ours.
commonMistakes.correct: Their timetable is similar to ours.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The whole team is responsible of preparing the room.
commonMistakes.correct: The whole team is responsible for preparing the room.
commonMistakes.why: Responsible for introduces an assigned duty.

commonMistakes.incorrect: My cousin is married with an architect.
commonMistakes.correct: My cousin is married to an architect.
commonMistakes.why: Married to names a spouse; married with can introduce details of a family.

studyTips: Build adjective cards with a complete short phrase on each: afraid of heights, good at cooking and interested in music.
Separate adjectives that sound related but take different prepositions: dependent on versus independent of; crowded with versus full of.
Read each practice sentence aloud with its preposition and replace the noun with a new noun or -ing activity.

exercises.prompt: Although she has never performed on stage, Alina is very interested ___ acting.
exercises.feedback: Interested in expresses curiosity about an activity; skill would be good at acting.

exercises.prompt: After three months of practice, Theo has become quite good ___ fixing bicycles.
exercises.feedback: Good at is the fixed adjective phrase for ability; fixing is an -ing activity.

exercises.prompt: The volunteers were proud ___ what they had achieved together.
exercises.feedback: Proud of introduces an achievement that gives someone satisfaction.

exercises.prompt: The community centre is dependent ___ donations to keep its classes free.
exercises.feedback: Dependent on names the support needed for continued operation.

exercises.prompt: The new badge looks very similar ___ the old design. (Supply the required preposition.)
acceptedAnswers: to
exercises.feedback: Similar to is the standard phrase for resemblance.

exercises.prompt: We need somebody who is capable ___ organising the entire event. (Supply one preposition.)
acceptedAnswers: of
exercises.feedback: Capable of is followed by a noun or an -ing verb naming the activity.

exercises.prompt: The coordinator is responsible ___ updating the attendance list. (Supply one preposition.)
acceptedAnswers: for
exercises.feedback: Responsible for names a duty assigned to a person.

exercises.prompt: The small hall was crowded ___ guests waiting for the talk. (Supply one preposition.)
acceptedAnswers: with
exercises.feedback: Crowded with describes a place occupied by many people or objects.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I am not very good in remembering phone numbers.
acceptedAnswers: I am not very good at remembering phone numbers.
exercises.feedback: The adjective good takes at before a skill or activity.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Everyone was aware for the change in the meeting time.
acceptedAnswers: Everyone was aware of the change in the meeting time.
exercises.feedback: Aware of introduces a fact or circumstance someone knows about.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: My parents are independent on financial support from relatives.
acceptedAnswers: My parents are independent of financial support from relatives.
exercises.feedback: Independent of means not needing support; dependent on means needing it.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Jules is married with a professional photographer.
acceptedAnswers: Jules is married to a professional photographer.
exercises.feedback: Married to introduces the spouse, not married with.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make one complete sentence with these facts: the volunteers / proud / their work. Begin with "The volunteers are".
acceptedAnswers: The volunteers are proud of their work.
speakingExercises.feedback: Proud of identifies the achievement or work that gives satisfaction.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend asks whether Iris can repair bicycles well. She can. Reply in one sentence beginning "Iris is good" and ending "repairing bicycles".
acceptedAnswers: Iris is good at repairing bicycles.
speakingExercises.feedback: Good at + -ing describes competence in an activity.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct only the adjective preposition and say the whole sentence: "This pattern is similar with that one."
acceptedAnswers: This pattern is similar to that one.
speakingExercises.feedback: Similar to is the standard construction for resemblance.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change "The editor must check every article" into one sentence beginning "The editor is responsible" and ending "every article". Use "checking".
acceptedAnswers: The editor is responsible for checking every article.
speakingExercises.feedback: Responsible for followed by an -ing verb names a duty.

speakingExercises.prompt: Nina wants to learn astronomy but has no experience yet. Say exactly "Nina is interested" followed by the correct preposition and "astronomy".
acceptedAnswers: Nina is interested in astronomy.
speakingExercises.feedback: Interested in describes curiosity rather than existing skill.

speakingExercises.prompt: Describe this fact in one complete sentence: the park / famous / its rose garden. Begin with "The park".
acceptedAnswers: The park is famous for its rose garden.
speakingExercises.feedback: Famous for identifies the feature associated with a place’s reputation.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say two sentences in this order. First: "The room" / full / books. Second: "The corridor" / crowded / visitors. Use "is" in both sentences.
acceptedAnswers: The room is full of books. The corridor is crowded with visitors.
speakingExercises.feedback: Full of and crowded with describe two different states with different prepositions.

speakingExercises.prompt: You do not have enough time to finish a task. Say one complete sentence beginning "I am short" and ending "time".
acceptedAnswers: I am short of time.
I'm short of time.
speakingExercises.feedback: Short of identifies a resource you do not have enough of.

listeningExercises.audioText: Maya loves learning new languages, but she is not very good at remembering vocabulary yet.
listeningExercises.feedback: Good at describes ability: Maya is interested in languages but struggles with vocabulary recall.

listeningExercises.audioText: The two jackets look similar, but the blue one is different from the green one in its material.
choices: The fabric they are made from
listeningExercises.feedback: Different from signals a contrast, and the audio identifies the material.

listeningExercises.audioText: The gardeners are proud of the flowers they grew for the spring festival.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word adjective–preposition phrase heard immediately after "are".
acceptedAnswers: proud of
listeningExercises.feedback: Proud of introduces the source of the gardeners’ satisfaction.

listeningExercises.audioText: Nora is responsible for setting up the microphones. Ben is in charge of welcoming the guests.
listeningExercises.feedback: Responsible for identifies Nora’s task: setting up the microphones.

listeningExercises.audioText: Our little café is famous for its lemon cake, although the owner is more proud of the bread.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which item attracts the café’s reputation?
listeningExercises.feedback: Famous for identifies the cake, while proud of names the owner’s personal preference.

listeningExercises.audioText: The waiting room was crowded with passengers, but the small office next door was almost empty.
listeningExercises.prompt: What was the waiting room like?
choices: It was closed to the public.
listeningExercises.feedback: Crowded with shows that the room contained many passengers, unlike the office.

listeningExercises.audioText: The children are keen on joining the after-school photography club.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word adjective–preposition phrase immediately after "are".
acceptedAnswers: keen on
listeningExercises.feedback: Keen on expresses enthusiasm for an activity or proposal.

listeningExercises.audioText: Our organisation is short of volunteers for the weekend event.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word adjective–preposition phrase immediately after "is".
acceptedAnswers: short of
listeningExercises.feedback: Short of indicates that the organisation does not have enough volunteers.
